item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine launched drones that hit Russia's largest oil refinery in Siberia, while Russian forces killed a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker in a drone strike and downed a Ukrainian drone in Russia's Smolensk region, killing two people. Russia reported intercepting 146 drones in the Leningrad region and a drone that wounded three energy workers in Sumy Oblast. A U.S.-mediated prisoner swap was concluded in Abu Dhabi, but broader peace talks ended without a breakthrough. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has continued to target U.S. assets, striking a radar site in Bahrain and launching drones that were shot down, while the United States has responded by striking Iran's Qeshm Island and disabling a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman. Iran also hit a building in Tel Aviv with a missile and opened a women’s war-readiness training camp, and it designated the Argentine navy and air force as terrorist organisations and warned of retaliation against European bases hosting U.S. forces. Qatar reported progress in U.S., Iran talks after a White House meeting, and France blamed Iran for a cyberattack on refrigeration systems. Defense spending is being constrained by the standoff, and 123 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

Unidentified gunmen killed one Syrian soldier and wounded two in eastern Deir ez-Zor, with similar attacks reported in Jadidat Bakara. Lebanon has asked Syria to extradite suspects linked to the killing of an ex-Iraqi MP. Syrian security officials are restructuring the army and preparing new security and administrative changes. item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army has seized the towns of Bakori and Sali in West Kordofan while continuing offensives that recaptured Al-Khuwai and other areas in West and North Kordofan from the RSF. The RSF has intensified drone strikes, killing nine civilians in the Blue Nile and accounting for two thirds of child casualties in the conflict. An RSF drone was downed by the army in the south, reportedly launched from Ethiopia. A senior RSF commander defected to the army after 13 years of service, and Vinícius Jr of Real Madrid sent a video message to a boy who received prosthetic legs after a drone strike. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
UN peacekeepers were accused of failing to protect civilians before the Abiemnom massacre that killed at least 213 people, prompting Amnesty International to call for investigations of the authorities and the UN. Clashes continue between government forces and opposition fighters in Akobo while governors in Jonglei and Aweil East urge peace ahead of elections scheduled for next month, which envoys warn could unravel fragile stability. A convoy ambush in South Sudan killed two people, including a journalist, and a CityLink Aviation plane crashed near Juba killing all 14 aboard. The humanitarian situation deepens with hunger, displacement and ongoing sexual violence, and 2 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Federal forces have captured additional Tigray cities while fighting continues, and severe drought and prolonged conflict are driving acute hunger in Amhara, Tigray and Afar. Ethiopian drones are now operating over Sudan and RSF drones are launching from Ethiopian territory against Sudanese targets, prompting diplomatic expulsions and consular closures. An RPG strike near a school in Moyale killed dozens of Ethiopian Orthodox believers and a Kenyan, and attacks on Orthodox Christians persist in Arsi, Benishangul Gumuz and the north, with blasts heard in Addis Ababa. Seed insecurity threatens Tigray farmers and a psychosocial and spiritual care pilot is being tested, while displacement exceeds 50,000 people, and 2,824 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

In northern Nigeria, violence forced tens of thousands of civilians to flee into Niger and opposition leader Atiku accused President Tinubu of failing Nigerians after 638 people were killed and 64,000 fled. item.title: The Philippines: the situation
item.description:

Former NPA rebels were redeployed as forest guards to protect Borongan’s environment, and intelligence cooperation was boosted through a workshop by 10ID and partners. 176 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
